plans.note: Section 9 is the dedicated liability clause; check mutuality, cap amount (likely tied to fees paid), and carve-outs, and confirm the indemnity in Section 8 (sec-8-2) and warranty disclaimers in Section 7 (sec-8) are excluded from the cap.

Section 8 (sec-8-2) should carry Commerce One's IP infringement indemnity in our favour as licensee/host; verify defence control, no dilution by the Section 9 cap, and that any Corio-side indemnity (including trademark use under Section 6) stays narrow.

Restrictions on the businesses we may pursue are most likely embedded in the grant of rights (sec-3) and in the CORIO MARKET SEGMENT / TERRITORY definitions (sec-1-2), with possible marketing-cooperation constraints in Exhibit D (sec-20).

Check the grant of rights (sec-3) and market-segment/territory definitions (sec-1-2) for any obligation to host or resell only Commerce One software; Exhibit D (sec-20) and shared resources (sec-13) may add de facto exclusivity.

Any most-favoured-pricing language would sit in Section 4 fees or the Exhibit B pricing/revenue-sharing terms; confirm no obligation running from us to Commerce One, and seek an MFN in our favour if pricing is volume/revenue based.

No dedicated personnel clause in the outline; if a non-solicit exists it would be in Miscellaneous (sec-14) or the shared resources provision (sec-13) covering seconded staff and relationship managers.

Section 11 governs term and termination; confirm we have a convenience exit on notice without penalty and that Commerce One cannot terminate mid-term other than for uncured material breach, and check Section 4 for any acceleration of fees on exit.
Auto-renewal mechanics and non-renewal notice windows belong in Section 11; cross-check renewal pricing/uplift caps against Section 4 and the Exhibit B pricing schedule.

Governing law, venue and any dispute/arbitration mechanism (note the defined term RULES, suggesting arbitration rules) will be in Miscellaneous (sec-14) with the definition in sec-1-2; confirm an accepted jurisdiction and court forum.

Assignment and change-of-control language is standard in Miscellaneous (sec-14); ensure we may assign to affiliates and successors and that Commerce One has no termination right in Section 11 triggered by our change of control.

Ownership provisions likely sit in the grant of rights (sec-3) and the DEVELOPMENTS / EMPLOYEE NDA-INVENTION definitions (sec-1-2); confirm we retain our platform, customer data and configurations, with escrow (sec-12), trademark (sec-6) and confidentiality (sec-10) cross-checks.

Section 2 grant of rights (sec-3) plus delivery (sec-3-2) and the Exhibit A software list (sec-1-3, sec-2) define scope; confirm the licence is irrevocable for the term, covers our affiliates, contractors and hosted Customers/Software Users, and matches TERRITORY.

Usage-reporting and audit rights in a revenue-share model typically appear in Section 4 fees or Exhibit B payment terms (sec-17); seek notice, frequency limits, off-site review and Commerce One bearing its own costs.

Check Section 4 and Exhibit B payment terms (sec-17) for late-payment interest or penalty amounts payable by us, and the support exhibit (sec-18/sec-p0171) for any credits or penalties; credits should run to us, not against us.

Section 7 warranties and disclaimer (sec-8) is the primary location; test the Warranty Period and Acceptance Test definitions (sec-1-2), the delivery/acceptance mechanics (sec-3-2) and maintenance obligations (sec-5) for a real repair-or-refund remedy.

No insurance section appears in the outline; if added it would sit in Miscellaneous (sec-14) near the indemnity (sec-8-2), and is a lower priority here since Commerce One licenses software rather than accessing our premises.

Minimum fees, guaranteed revenue-share floors or implementation-fee commitments would appear in Section 4 and Exhibit B pricing/revenue-sharing (sec-p0148, sec-p0155, sec-17); confirm any minimum has an exit or reduction right.

Post-termination effects should be in Section 11 (wind-down for hosted Customers, data return, survival); the source code escrow (sec-12) and confidentiality return obligations (sec-10) support continuity, and we may need a run-off licence under sec-3.
